notes: Hand-written, kid-friendly facts: foods, inventions, famous people, exports and fun history. No war, crime, death, alcohol or adult topics. Keys: countries = country name without a leading 'the'; capitals = capital name; stateCapitals = 'Capital, State'. Keep each under ~150 characters so it fits the result card. Fact-check before launch.

countries.Algeria: Algeria is Africa's biggest country. Couscous is a favorite dish, and sweet dates from its desert oases are shipped all over the world.
countries.Angola: Angola's Kalandula Falls are among the biggest waterfalls in Africa. Funge, a smooth cassava porridge, is a favorite meal.
countries.Benin: Benin's Ganvié is a whole village built on stilts in a lake, where people get around by canoe. Cotton is one of its biggest exports.
countries.Botswana: Botswana is one of the world's top diamond producers, and its Okavango Delta is home to huge herds of elephants.
countries.Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso's name means 'land of honest people.' It hosts FESPACO, the biggest film festival in Africa.
countries.Burundi: Burundi's royal drummers are so famous that their drumming is protected as a world treasure by UNESCO. Coffee and tea are top exports.
countries.Cabo Verde: Cabo Verde is a chain of volcanic islands. Singer Cesária Évora, the 'Barefoot Diva,' came from here. Cachupa stew is the national dish.
countries.Cameroon: Cameroon is called 'Africa in miniature' because it has beaches, deserts, mountains and rainforest. Football star Samuel Eto'o is from here.
countries.Central African Republic: The Central African Republic's rainforests are home to forest elephants and lowland gorillas. It sits right in the middle of Africa.
countries.Chad: Chad is named after Lake Chad. Its Ennedi Plateau has giant natural rock arches and ancient rock paintings of cattle and camels.
countries.Comoros: The Comoros grow much of the world's ylang-ylang, a sweet-smelling flower used in perfume. Vanilla and cloves are big exports too.
countries.Republic of the Congo: The Republic of the Congo is mostly rainforest and is home to many western lowland gorillas. Cassava is the main food crop.
countries.Democratic Republic of the Congo: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has Africa's second-biggest rainforest and is the only home of the okapi, a striped cousin of the giraffe.
countries.Ivory Coast (Côte d'Ivoire): Ivory Coast grows more cocoa beans than any other country, so lots of the world's chocolate starts here. Football star Didier Drogba is from here.
countries.Djibouti: Djibouti's Lake Assal is one of the saltiest lakes on Earth and the lowest point in Africa.
countries.Egypt: Egypt is home to the Great Pyramid of Giza, the only Ancient Wonder still standing. Ancient Egyptians made papyrus, one of the first kinds of paper.
countries.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in Africa where Spanish is an official language. Sea turtles nest on the beaches of Bioko Island.
countries.Eritrea: Eritrea's capital, Asmara, is famous for its colorful 1930s buildings. Injera, a spongy flatbread, is eaten with most meals.
countries.Eswatini: Eswatini's Umhlanga Reed Dance is a famous colorful festival. Sugar from its sugarcane fields is its biggest export.
countries.Ethiopia: Legend says coffee was discovered in Ethiopia by a goat herder named Kaldi, whose goats got extra bouncy after eating the berries.
countries.Gabon: Almost 90% of Gabon is covered in rainforest, home to forest elephants and gorillas. Some of its elephants even surf the waves!
countries.Gambia: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa, a thin strip along the Gambia River. Peanuts are its main crop.
countries.Ghana: Ghana is one of the world's top cocoa growers, and its colorful kente cloth is famous worldwide. Jollof rice is a favorite dish.
countries.Guinea: Guinea has some of the world's biggest supplies of bauxite, used to make aluminum. The Niger River starts in its green highlands.
countries.Guinea-Bissau: Guinea-Bissau's Bijagós Islands are home to rare hippos that swim in the sea. Cashew nuts are its biggest export.
countries.Kenya: Kenya's runners have won loads of Olympic medals, and the Maasai Mara hosts the Great Migration of wildebeest. Tea is a top export.
countries.Lesotho: Lesotho is completely surrounded by South Africa, and all of its land is over 4,500 feet high, so it's called the 'Kingdom in the Sky.'
countries.Liberia: Liberia was founded in 1847 and is Africa's oldest republic. Rubber from its huge plantations is a major export.
countries.Libya: More than 90% of Libya is desert. The ancient Roman city of Leptis Magna has some of the best-kept ruins in the world.
countries.Madagascar: Madagascar is the only place on Earth where lemurs live in the wild, and it grows most of the world's vanilla.
countries.Malawi: Lake Malawi has more kinds of fish than any other lake on Earth. Malawi is nicknamed 'the Warm Heart of Africa.'
countries.Mali: Mali's Great Mosque of Djenné is the biggest mud-brick building in the world. Mansa Musa of Mali is often called the richest person in history.
countries.Mauritania: Mauritania's Richat Structure, nicknamed the 'Eye of the Sahara,' is a giant ring in the desert you can see from space.
countries.Mauritius: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo bird, now its national symbol. Its 'Seven Colored Earth' sand dunes are striped like a rainbow.
countries.Morocco: Morocco is famous for tagine stews and mint tea. The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez is often called the oldest university in the world.
countries.Mozambique: Mozambique has more than 1,500 miles of Indian Ocean coastline, and its peri-peri chili sauce is loved around the world.
countries.Namibia: Namibia's red Sossusvlei sand dunes are some of the tallest in the world. It was one of the first countries to protect nature in its constitution.
countries.Niger: Niger hosts the Cure Salée, a colorful festival where herders gather with their camels and cattle at the end of the rainy season.
countries.Nigeria: Nigeria has more people than any other African country, and its film industry, Nollywood, makes thousands of movies. Jollof rice is a favorite.
countries.Rwanda: Rwanda is called the 'Land of a Thousand Hills,' and its misty mountain forests are home to rare mountain gorillas.
countries.São Tomé and Príncipe: São Tomé and Príncipe sits almost exactly on the equator and grows some of the finest cocoa in the world.
countries.Senegal: Senegal's Lake Retba is bright pink! Thieboudienne, a dish of fish with rice and vegetables, is the national meal.
countries.Seychelles: The Seychelles' coco de mer palm grows the biggest seed of any plant, and giant tortoises roam its islands.
countries.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone is famous for its white sand beaches, and Tiwai Island is home to pygmy hippos and many kinds of monkeys.
countries.Somalia: Somalia has the longest coastline on mainland Africa and more camels than any other country in the world.
countries.South Africa: South Africa has three capital cities and 12 official languages. Nelson Mandela, winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, was its president.
countries.South Sudan: South Sudan became the world's newest country in 2011. Its grasslands host one of the biggest antelope migrations on Earth.
countries.Sudan: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt, built by the kings of Kush. The Blue Nile and White Nile meet here.
countries.Tanzania: Tanzania is home to Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti. Its island of Zanzibar is famous for spices like cloves.
countries.Togo: In Togo's Koutammakou region, families live in tall, two-story mud tower houses called takienta.
countries.Tunisia: Parts of the Star Wars movies were filmed in Tunisia's desert. It's famous for olive oil and couscous.
countries.Uganda: Uganda is called the 'Pearl of Africa.' It borders Lake Victoria, Africa's biggest lake, and is home to about half of the world's mountain gorillas.
countries.Zambia: Zambia shares Victoria Falls with Zimbabwe. Locals call it 'the smoke that thunders.' Copper is its biggest export.
countries.Zimbabwe: Great Zimbabwe, a huge stone city built about 800 years ago, gave the country its name. It shares Victoria Falls with Zambia.
countries.Afghanistan: Afghanistan is famous for juicy pomegranates and saffron. The lakes of Band-e Amir are a brilliant blue.
countries.Armenia: Armenia was the first country to make Christianity its official religion, in 301 AD. Apricots are so loved here they're a national symbol.
countries.Azerbaijan: Azerbaijan is called the 'Land of Fire' because natural gas flames burn right out of its hillsides. Plov, a rice dish, is a favorite.
countries.Bahrain: Bahrain is famous for its history of pearl diving. Its 'Tree of Life' has grown alone in the desert for about 400 years.
countries.Bangladesh: Bangladesh has the Sundarbans, the world's biggest mangrove forest and home of the Bengal tiger. It's a top maker of clothes.
countries.Bhutan: Bhutan measures success with 'Gross National Happiness.' Its national dish, ema datshi, is chili peppers cooked in cheese.
countries.Brunei: Brunei's Kampong Ayer is a huge village built on stilts over the water, with its own schools and shops.
countries.Cambodia: Cambodia's Angkor Wat is the biggest religious monument in the world, and it's even pictured on the country's flag.
countries.China: China invented paper, the compass and fireworks. The Great Wall stretches thousands of miles, and dumplings are a favorite food.
countries.Georgia: Khachapuri, a boat-shaped bread filled with melted cheese and egg, is Georgia's most famous dish. The Caucasus Mountains run across it.
countries.India: India gave the world chess and the number zero as we use it today. It's the world's biggest spice grower, and curry is loved everywhere.
countries.Indonesia: Indonesia has more than 17,000 islands and is the only home of the Komodo dragon. Nasi goreng, fried rice, is a national favorite.
countries.Iran: Iran, once called Persia, is famous for handmade carpets and saffron. The poet Hafez, from the city of Shiraz, is still loved today.
countries.Iraq: Iraq is home to ancient Mesopotamia, where people invented one of the first forms of writing. Dates from its palm trees are famous.
countries.Israel: Israel's Dead Sea is so salty you float like a cork. Drip irrigation, a clever way to water crops, was developed here.
countries.Japan: Japan is famous for sushi, ramen and super-fast bullet trains. Super Mario and Pokémon were created here.
countries.Jordan: Jordan's ancient city of Petra was carved right into pink rock cliffs. Mansaf, lamb with rice and yogurt sauce, is the national dish.
countries.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan is the world's biggest landlocked country. Apples first grew wild here, and the first person in space launched from here.
countries.Kuwait: Kuwait's famous Kuwait Towers are covered in shiny blue and green discs. Machboos, spiced rice with meat, is a favorite dish.
countries.Kyrgyzstan: More than 90% of Kyrgyzstan is mountains. Many families still spend summers in felt tents called yurts, and horse games are a big part of festivals.
countries.Laos: Laos is famous for sticky rice, which people roll into little balls and eat with their hands. Its Kuang Si Falls have turquoise pools.
countries.Lebanon: The cedar tree on Lebanon's flag has grown in its mountains for thousands of years. Hummus and tabbouleh are favorite foods.
countries.Malaysia: Malaysia's Petronas Towers were once the tallest buildings in the world. Nasi lemak, rice cooked in coconut milk, is the national dish.
countries.Maldives: The Maldives is the lowest country in the world, made of about 1,200 coral islands. Its waters are famous for manta rays.
countries.Mongolia: Mongolia has more horses than people, and many families live in round felt tents called gers. Cashmere wool is a top export.
countries.Myanmar: Myanmar is called the 'Golden Land' for its thousands of golden pagodas. Mohinga, a fish noodle soup, is a favorite breakfast.
countries.Nepal: Nepal is home to Mount Everest and eight of the world's 10 tallest mountains. Momo dumplings are a favorite snack.
countries.North Korea: North Korea's Mount Paektu has a beautiful crater lake on top. Cold buckwheat noodles called naengmyeon are a famous dish.
countries.Oman: Oman is famous for frankincense, a sweet-smelling tree sap people have traded for thousands of years. Its mountains are full of old forts.
countries.Pakistan: Pakistan is home to K2, the world's second-tallest mountain. Many of the world's hand-stitched footballs are made in its city of Sialkot.
countries.Palestine: Palestine is famous for its olive trees and olive oil, and for dresses with colorful hand-stitched embroidery. Knafeh is a well-loved sweet.
countries.Philippines: The Philippines has more than 7,600 islands. It's famous for jeepneys, colorful buses, and adobo, a tangy stewed dish.
countries.Qatar: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first in the Arab world. Some of its sand dunes 'sing' with a humming sound in the wind.
countries.Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia has the Rub' al Khali, the biggest sand desert in the world. Guests are welcomed with dates and Arabic coffee.
countries.Singapore: Singapore is a city and a country at the same time. Its Gardens by the Bay have giant glowing 'supertrees,' and its food stalls are famous.
countries.South Korea: South Korea is famous for kimchi, K-pop and smartphones. King Sejong created the Korean alphabet, Hangul, in the 1400s.
countries.Sri Lanka: Sri Lanka is one of the world's top tea growers, famous for Ceylon tea. Elephants and spicy curries are part of everyday life.
countries.Syria: Syria's capital, Damascus, is one of the oldest cities in the world. Aleppo soap, made with olive and laurel oil, is famous.
countries.Taiwan: Taiwan makes many of the world's computer chips, and bubble tea was invented here. Taipei 101 was once the tallest building in the world.
countries.Tajikistan: More than 90% of Tajikistan is mountains, including the Pamirs, called the 'Roof of the World.' Plov rice is a favorite meal.
countries.Thailand: Thailand is famous for pad thai and mango sticky rice. The elephant is a national symbol, and it's one of the world's top rice exporters.
countries.Timor-Leste: Timor-Leste became independent in 2002 and is famous for its coffee. Its coral reefs have some of the most kinds of fish on Earth.
countries.Türkiye (Turkey): Tulips were grown in gardens in Türkiye long before they became famous in the Netherlands. Turkish delight and baklava are famous sweets.
countries.Turkmenistan: Turkmenistan's Akhal-Teke horses have shiny golden coats, and a giant natural gas crater in its desert has been burning since 1971.
countries.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates is home to the Burj Khalifa, the tallest building in the world. Dubai even has an indoor ski slope in the desert.
countries.Uzbekistan: Uzbekistan's cities of Samarkand and Bukhara were famous stops on the Silk Road trade route. Plov is the national dish.
countries.Vietnam: Vietnam is famous for pho noodle soup and is one of the world's top coffee growers. Ha Long Bay has nearly 2,000 limestone islands.
countries.Yemen: Yemen's town of Shibam has mud-brick tower houses, nicknamed the 'Manhattan of the desert.' Mocha coffee is named after Yemen's port of Mocha.
countries.Albania: Albania's sunny coast is called the Albanian Riviera, and its old city of Berat is known as the 'town of a thousand windows.'
countries.Andorra: Andorra is a tiny country high in the Pyrenees mountains, famous for skiing. It doesn't have an airport.
countries.Austria: Austria was home to the composers Mozart and Strauss. Wiener schnitzel and apple strudel are its famous dishes.
countries.Belarus: Belarus has huge ancient forests where European bison roam. Draniki, crispy potato pancakes, are the national dish.
countries.Belgium: Belgium is famous for chocolate, waffles and fries. The comic heroes Tintin and the Smurfs were created here.
countries.Bosnia and Herzegovina: Bosnia and Herzegovina's Stari Most is a famous old stone bridge in Mostar where divers leap into the river. Ćevapi are a favorite food.
countries.Bulgaria: Bulgaria's Valley of Roses makes much of the world's rose oil, used in perfume. Bulgarian yogurt is famous too.
countries.Croatia: Croatia gave the world the necktie! Its Plitvice Lakes are a chain of 16 turquoise lakes linked by waterfalls.
countries.Cyprus: Cyprus is the legendary birthplace of the goddess Aphrodite. Halloumi, a squeaky cheese you can grill, comes from here.
countries.Czechia (Czech Republic): Czechia has more castles than almost anywhere in Europe. The sugar cube and soft contact lenses were invented here.
countries.Denmark: Denmark gave the world LEGO bricks and the fairy tales of Hans Christian Andersen, like The Little Mermaid.
countries.Estonia: Estonia is one of the world's most digital countries, and Skype was created here. It has more than 2,000 islands.
countries.Finland: Finland has about 188,000 lakes and around 3 million saunas. The game Angry Birds was made here.
countries.France: France invented the hot air balloon and is famous for croissants and cheese. The Eiffel Tower is one of the world's most visited landmarks.
countries.Germany: Johannes Gutenberg's printing press and Karl Benz's first car were both invented in Germany. Pretzels are a favorite snack.
countries.Greece: Ancient Greece started the Olympic Games and gave the world democracy. Olive oil and feta cheese are famous Greek foods.
countries.Hungary: Hungary is where Ernő Rubik invented the Rubik's Cube in 1974. Goulash, a paprika stew, is the national dish.
countries.Iceland: Iceland is the land of fire and ice, full of volcanoes, glaciers and geysers. The word 'geyser' comes from Iceland's Geysir.
countries.Ireland: Ireland is called the Emerald Isle for its green fields. Halloween grew out of Samhain, an ancient Irish festival.
countries.Italy: Italy is the home of pizza and pasta, and of artists Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo. It has more World Heritage Sites than any other country.
countries.Kosovo: Kosovo became independent in 2008, making it one of Europe's youngest countries. Flija, a layered pancake pie, is a traditional dish.
countries.Latvia: About half of Latvia is covered in forest. Latvians have collected more than a million traditional folk songs called dainas.
countries.Liechtenstein: Liechtenstein is one of the smallest countries in the world, and also one of the world's biggest makers of false teeth!
countries.Lithuania: Lithuania is famous for amber, golden fossilized tree sap from the Baltic Sea. Cepelinai, big potato dumplings, are the national dish.
countries.Luxembourg: Luxembourg is one of the smallest countries in Europe. Its capital is built on cliffs with fortress walls and tunnels.
countries.North Macedonia: North Macedonia's Lake Ohrid is one of the oldest and deepest lakes in Europe, with fish found nowhere else.
countries.Malta: Malta's ancient temples are older than the pyramids of Egypt and Stonehenge. Pastizzi, flaky pastries, are a favorite snack.
countries.Moldova: Moldova is famous for its colorful embroidery and folk dances. Mămăligă, a golden cornmeal porridge, is a traditional dish.
countries.Monaco: Monaco is the world's second-smallest country and hosts the Monaco Grand Prix, a famous car race through its streets.
countries.Montenegro: Montenegro means 'Black Mountain.' The Bay of Kotor is ringed by dramatic mountains and old stone towns.
countries.Netherlands: The Netherlands is famous for tulips, windmills and wooden shoes, and about a quarter of it is below sea level. Vincent van Gogh was born here.
countries.Norway: Norway is famous for fjords and the northern lights. The cheese slicer was invented here, and Norwegian salmon is sold worldwide.
countries.Poland: Polish astronomer Copernicus showed that the Earth goes around the Sun. Pierogi dumplings are a favorite dish.
countries.Portugal: Portugal's explorers sailed around Africa to reach India. It's famous for custard tarts and makes more cork than any other country.
countries.Romania: Romania's Carpathian Mountains are home to many of Europe's brown bears. Romanian inventor Petrache Poenaru patented the fountain pen.
countries.Russia: Russia is the biggest country on Earth, spanning 11 time zones. It launched Sputnik, the first satellite, and Yuri Gagarin, the first person in space.
countries.San Marino: San Marino, founded in 301 AD, is one of the oldest republics in the world. It sits on top of Mount Titano.
countries.Serbia: Serbia is one of the world's top raspberry growers. Tennis star Novak Djokovic grew up here.
countries.Slovakia: Slovakia has lots of castles and caves. Bryndzové halušky, potato dumplings with sheep cheese, is the national dish.
countries.Slovenia: More than half of Slovenia is forest. Lake Bled has a tiny island with a church that you can row out to.
countries.Spain: Spain is famous for paella and tapas, and for the artist Pablo Picasso. The mop and the Chupa Chups lollipop were invented here.
countries.Sweden: Sweden gave the world IKEA, the band ABBA and the Nobel Prizes, started by Alfred Nobel. Meatballs are a classic dish.
countries.Switzerland: Switzerland is famous for chocolate, cheese and watches. Velcro was invented here, inspired by burrs stuck to a dog's fur.
countries.Ukraine: Ukraine is one of the world's biggest growers of sunflowers and wheat. Borscht, a bright red beet soup, is a famous dish.
countries.United Kingdom: The UK is home to Shakespeare and the Beatles, and British scientist Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web. Fish and chips is a classic.
countries.Vatican City: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world, completely surrounded by the city of Rome.
countries.Antigua and Barbuda: Antigua and Barbuda says it has 365 beaches, one for every day of the year. Cricket is the most popular sport.
countries.Bahamas: The Bahamas has about 700 islands, and on one of them you can swim with pigs! Conch salad is a favorite dish.
countries.Barbados: Barbados is the birthplace of singer Rihanna and of the grapefruit, which first appeared here in the 1700s.
countries.Belize: Belize's Great Blue Hole is a giant underwater sinkhole you can see from the sky. It has the second-biggest barrier reef in the world.
countries.Canada: Canada has the longest coastline of any country and makes most of the world's maple syrup. Basketball was invented by Canadian James Naismith.
countries.Costa Rica: Costa Rica protects about a quarter of its land as parks, full of sloths and toucans. It's a top grower of pineapples and bananas.
countries.Cuba: Cuba is the biggest island in the Caribbean, famous for salsa music and colorful classic cars. Its national bird has the colors of its flag.
countries.Dominica: Dominica is called the 'Nature Isle,' and it has a Boiling Lake, one of the biggest hot lakes in the world.
countries.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic is famous for merengue music and baseball. Many Major League stars grew up here.
countries.El Salvador: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America and is famous for pupusas, thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese or beans.
countries.Grenada: Grenada is called the 'Spice Isle' because it grows so much nutmeg. There's even a nutmeg on its flag!
countries.Guatemala: Guatemala was a heart of the ancient Maya, whose city of Tikal has giant pyramids. People here were making chocolate drinks thousands of years ago.
countries.Haiti: Haiti became independent in 1804, the second country in the Americas to do so. Its brightly painted 'tap-tap' buses are rolling works of art.
countries.Honduras: Honduras has the ancient Maya city of Copán, famous for its carved stone staircase. Baleadas, tortillas with beans, are a favorite.
countries.Jamaica: Jamaica is the home of reggae music and Bob Marley, and of sprinter Usain Bolt, the fastest person ever timed.
countries.Mexico: Mexico gave the world chocolate, corn and chili peppers, and tacos are loved everywhere. Chichén Itzá is a famous Maya pyramid.
countries.Nicaragua: Nicaragua is called the 'land of lakes and volcanoes.' Lake Nicaragua even has sharks that swim in fresh water!
countries.Panama: The Panama Canal lets ships cross between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Fun twist: the 'Panama hat' is actually from Ecuador!
countries.Saint Kitts and Nevis: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest country in the Americas. An old sugar-cane railway now gives visitors scenic rides around the island.
countries.Saint Lucia: Saint Lucia's twin Pitons are tall volcanic peaks rising from the sea, and it has a 'drive-in' volcano with bubbling mud baths.
countries.Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is a chain of 32 islands, and it's one of the world's top growers of arrowroot, used in cooking.
countries.Trinidad and Tobago: Trinidad and Tobago invented the steelpan drum, made from oil barrels. Its Carnival is one of the biggest in the world.
countries.United States: The Wright brothers flew the first airplane in the United States, and Americans landed the first people on the Moon in 1969.
countries.Argentina: Argentina is the birthplace of the tango and of football star Lionel Messi. Empanadas and dulce de leche are favorite treats.
countries.Bolivia: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni is the biggest salt flat in the world, and it turns into a giant mirror after it rains.
countries.Brazil: Brazil has most of the Amazon rainforest and has won the men's World Cup five times, more than any other country. It's the world's top coffee grower.
countries.Chile: Chile is one of the longest, skinniest countries on Earth. The giant moai statues of Easter Island belong to Chile.
countries.Colombia: Colombia is famous for coffee and emeralds, and has more kinds of birds than any other country. Singer Shakira is from here.
countries.Ecuador: Ecuador owns the Galápagos Islands, where Charles Darwin studied giant tortoises and finches. The 'Panama hat' is actually made here.
countries.Guyana: Guyana's Kaieteur Falls is one of the most powerful waterfalls in the world. It's the only English-speaking country in South America.
countries.Paraguay: Paraguay is famous for ñandutí lace, which looks like a spider web, and for sharing yerba mate tea with friends.
countries.Peru: Peru is home to Machu Picchu, an Inca city high in the mountains. Potatoes were first grown here thousands of years ago.
countries.Suriname: Suriname is the most forested country in the world, with over 90% of its land covered in trees. Dutch is its official language.
countries.Uruguay: Uruguay hosted and won the very first FIFA World Cup in 1930. Dulce de leche and asado barbecue are favorites.
countries.Venezuela: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the tallest waterfall in the world. Arepas, corn cakes stuffed with fillings, are eaten every day.
countries.Australia: Australia is the only country that's also a whole continent, home to kangaroos and koalas. Key Wi-Fi technology was invented here.
countries.Fiji: Fiji has more than 300 islands, and its rugby sevens team won Olympic gold medals in 2016 and 2021.
countries.Kiribati: Kiribati is the only country in all four hemispheres, and its Kiritimati island is one of the first places to welcome each New Year.
countries.Marshall Islands: The Marshall Islands are made of 29 coral atolls. Long ago, sailors here made ocean maps out of sticks and shells.
countries.Micronesia: Micronesia's Nan Madol is an ancient city built on little islands in a lagoon. On the island of Yap, giant stone discs were used as money.
countries.Nauru: Nauru is the world's smallest island country, only about 8 square miles. You can drive all the way around it in about 30 minutes.
countries.New Zealand: New Zealand is home to the kiwi bird and was the filming location for The Lord of the Rings. Edmund Hillary, an Everest pioneer, was from here.
countries.Palau: Palau's Jellyfish Lake is full of millions of golden jellyfish with very mild stings. Palau created the world's first shark sanctuary.
countries.Papua New Guinea: Papua New Guinea has more than 800 languages, more than any other country. A bird-of-paradise appears on its flag.
countries.Samoa: In 2011 Samoa jumped across the International Date Line and skipped a whole day! Rugby is the national sport.
countries.Solomon Islands: The Solomon Islands have more than 900 islands and amazing coral reefs. Shell money is still used in special ceremonies.
countries.Tonga: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom of about 170 islands, and humpback whales visit its warm waters every year to have their calves.
countries.Tuvalu: Tuvalu is one of the smallest countries in the world. Its internet ending, '.tv,' is used by TV websites everywhere and earns it money.
countries.Vanuatu: Vanuatu has an underwater post office where divers mail waterproof postcards. Mount Yasur is one of the most visited volcanoes on Earth.

capitals.Algiers: Algiers is nicknamed 'Algiers the White' for its white buildings climbing the hills above the Mediterranean Sea.
capitals.Luanda: Luanda's long seaside walkway, the Marginal, is a favorite spot for strolls along the bay.
capitals.Porto-Novo: Porto-Novo means 'New Port' in Portuguese. It's Benin's capital, while Cotonou is its biggest city.
capitals.Gaborone: Gaborone is one of the world's fastest-growing cities, with a nature reserve full of zebras and rhinos right nearby.
capitals.Ouagadougou: Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, the biggest film festival in Africa, every two years.
capitals.Gitega: Gitega became Burundi's capital in 2019 and is home to the country's National Museum.
capitals.Praia: Praia means 'beach' in Portuguese, and the old city sits on a flat hilltop above the ocean.
capitals.Yaoundé: Yaoundé is built across seven hills, so it's known as the 'City of Seven Hills.'
capitals.Bangui: Bangui sits on the Ubangi River, right across the water from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
capitals.N'Djamena: N'Djamena sits where the Chari and Logone rivers meet.
capitals.Moroni: Moroni sits on a volcanic island beside Mount Karthala, one of the biggest active volcanoes in the world.
capitals.Brazzaville: Brazzaville and Kinshasa face each other across the Congo River, making them the closest pair of capital cities on the mainland.
capitals.Kinshasa: Kinshasa is one of Africa's biggest cities and a home of soukous, a lively dance music played all over Africa.
capitals.Yamoussoukro: Yamoussoukro is the official capital, while Abidjan is the biggest city. Its giant basilica is one of the largest churches in the world.
capitals.Djibouti: Djibouti City is a busy port at the entrance to the Red Sea, where ships sail between Europe and Asia.
capitals.Cairo: Cairo is one of the biggest cities in Africa, and the Great Pyramids of Giza sit right at its edge.
capitals.Malabo: Malabo sits on Bioko Island, not on the mainland, surrounded by green volcanic hills.
capitals.Asmara: Asmara is famous for its colorful 1930s buildings, including a gas station shaped like an airplane.
capitals.Mbabane: Mbabane sits in green mountains with cool, misty weather.
capitals.Addis Ababa: Addis Ababa means 'new flower' and is home to the headquarters of the African Union.
capitals.Libreville: Libreville sits on the Atlantic coast just north of the equator, surrounded by rainforest.
capitals.Banjul: Banjul sits on an island right where the Gambia River meets the Atlantic Ocean.
capitals.Accra: Accra is famous for colorful markets and lively highlife music.
capitals.Conakry: Conakry is built on a narrow peninsula that sticks out into the Atlantic Ocean.
capitals.Bissau: Bissau's colorful Carnival is one of the biggest celebrations in West Africa.
capitals.Nairobi: Nairobi is the only capital city with a national park full of lions, giraffes and rhinos right at its edge.
capitals.Maseru: Maseru's craft center is built in the shape of a giant Basotho straw hat.
capitals.Monrovia: Monrovia is named after James Monroe, the fifth president of the United States.
capitals.Tripoli: Tripoli's old city has a Roman stone arch built nearly 2,000 years ago.
capitals.Antananarivo: Antananarivo means 'City of the Thousand' and sits on hills in the middle of Madagascar.
capitals.Lilongwe: Lilongwe is a garden city with a nature sanctuary right in the middle of town.
capitals.Bamako: Bamako sits on the Niger River and is famous for its music and stars like Salif Keita.
capitals.Nouakchott: Nouakchott grew from a small village into one of the biggest cities in the Sahara.
capitals.Port Louis: Port Louis has a lively central market and a museum showing the Blue Penny, one of the rarest stamps in the world.
capitals.Rabat: Rabat's Hassan Tower is part of a giant mosque that was started in the 1190s.
capitals.Maputo: Maputo is known for its wide avenues lined with purple jacaranda trees.
capitals.Windhoek: Windhoek sits high on a plateau in the middle of Namibia, and its name means 'windy corner.'
capitals.Niamey: Niamey sits on the Niger River and has a national museum with a zoo and craft workshops.
capitals.Abuja: Abuja replaced Lagos as Nigeria's capital in 1991. Its giant Zuma Rock is often called the 'Gateway to Abuja.'
capitals.Kigali: Kigali is known as one of the cleanest cities in Africa, and on one Saturday each month neighbors clean up together.
capitals.São Tomé: São Tomé is one of the smallest capitals in Africa, surrounded by cocoa farms.
capitals.Dakar: Dakar is the westernmost city on mainland Africa and was the finish line of the famous Paris–Dakar Rally.
capitals.Victoria: Victoria is one of the smallest capitals in the world, with a tiny silver clock tower in the middle of town.
capitals.Freetown: Freetown sits beside one of the world's biggest natural harbors, with green mountains rising behind it.
capitals.Mogadishu: Mogadishu has been a busy trading port on the Indian Ocean for more than 1,000 years.
capitals.Pretoria: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Pretoria turns purple every spring with jacaranda trees.
capitals.Juba: Juba sits on the banks of the White Nile and became a national capital in 2011.
capitals.Khartoum: Khartoum is where the Blue Nile and the White Nile meet to form the great Nile River.
capitals.Dodoma: Dodoma is Tanzania's official capital, while Dar es Salaam is the biggest city.
capitals.Lomé: Lomé is known for its Grand Marché, a huge market run mostly by women traders.
capitals.Tunis: Close to Tunis are the ruins of ancient Carthage, once one of the greatest trading cities of the Mediterranean.
capitals.Kampala: Kampala was first built on seven hills and sits near the shore of Lake Victoria.
capitals.Lusaka: Lusaka's Kabwata Cultural Village sells crafts made by artists from all over Zambia.
capitals.Harare: Harare is famous for its jacaranda trees, which turn the city purple every spring.
capitals.Kabul: Kabul's Babur's Gardens were laid out in the 1500s with terraces, fountains and fruit trees.
capitals.Yerevan: Yerevan is called the 'Pink City' for its pink stone buildings, and you can see Mount Ararat from its streets.
capitals.Baku: Baku's three Flame Towers light up at night to look like giant flickering flames.
capitals.Manama: Manama is a busy island city famous for its history of pearl trading.
capitals.Dhaka: Dhaka is called the 'Rickshaw Capital of the World,' with hundreds of thousands of colorful bicycle rickshaws.
capitals.Thimphu: Thimphu is one of the only capital cities in the world without any traffic lights.
capitals.Bandar Seri Begawan: Bandar Seri Begawan has a mosque with a shining golden dome and a whole water village of houses on stilts.
capitals.Phnom Penh: Phnom Penh sits where the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers meet, and its Royal Palace has a Silver Pagoda with a floor of silver tiles.
capitals.Beijing: Beijing's Forbidden City was home to Chinese emperors for about 500 years. Peking duck is the city's famous dish.
capitals.Tbilisi: Tbilisi is famous for natural hot-spring baths, and its name comes from the Georgian word for 'warm.'
capitals.New Delhi: New Delhi is home to India Gate, and the beautiful Taj Mahal is just a few hours' drive away.
capitals.Jakarta: Jakarta is one of the biggest cities in the world. Its National Monument is topped with a flame covered in gold.
capitals.Tehran: Tehran sits beneath the snowy Alborz Mountains, and its Milad Tower is one of the tallest towers in the world.
capitals.Baghdad: More than 1,000 years ago, Baghdad's House of Wisdom was one of the greatest centers of learning in the world.
capitals.Tokyo: Tokyo is the biggest city area in the world, and its Shibuya Crossing is one of the busiest crosswalks anywhere.
capitals.Amman: Amman was built on seven hills and has a Roman theater from about 1,800 years ago that still hosts shows.
capitals.Astana: Astana became Kazakhstan's capital in 1997. Its Baiterek Tower is shaped like a tree holding a golden egg.
capitals.Kuwait City: Kuwait City's famous Kuwait Towers are covered in thousands of shiny blue and green discs.
capitals.Bishkek: Bishkek is a leafy green city with snowcapped mountains you can see from its streets.
capitals.Vientiane: Vientiane sits on the Mekong River, and its golden Pha That Luang stupa is a national symbol of Laos.
capitals.Beirut: Beirut is one of the oldest cities in the world, with a seaside walkway called the Corniche.
capitals.Kuala Lumpur: Kuala Lumpur is home to the Petronas Twin Towers, joined by a skybridge high in the air.
capitals.Malé: Malé is a whole capital city squeezed onto one small coral island.
capitals.Ulaanbaatar: Ulaanbaatar is the coldest capital city in the world.
capitals.Naypyidaw: Myanmar moved its capital from Yangon to Naypyidaw in 2005. Some of its roads are 20 lanes wide!
capitals.Kathmandu: Kathmandu's valley has seven World Heritage Sites, and many Everest climbers start their journey here.
capitals.Pyongyang: Pyongyang sits on the Taedong River, and its name means 'flat land.'
capitals.Muscat: Muscat sits between rugged mountains and the sea, with a beautiful harbor guarded by old forts.
capitals.Islamabad: Islamabad was built in the 1960s as a planned capital, at the foot of the green Margalla Hills.
capitals.Manila: Manila Bay is famous for its sunsets, and the city's old walled area is called Intramuros.
capitals.Doha: Doha's Museum of Islamic Art sits on its own little island in the bay.
capitals.Riyadh: Riyadh's Kingdom Centre tower has a skybridge at the top with views across the desert city.
capitals.Singapore: Singapore's Merlion statue, half lion and half fish, is the city's famous symbol.
capitals.Seoul: Seoul has five royal palaces from Korea's Joseon kings and is a world center of K-pop.
capitals.Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte: Sri Lanka's official capital sits right next to Colombo, its biggest city.
capitals.Damascus: Damascus is often called the oldest capital city in the world where people have lived without a break.
capitals.Taipei: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010, and Taipei's night markets are famous for snacks.
capitals.Dushanbe: Dushanbe means 'Monday' in Tajik, because it grew from a village with a big Monday market.
capitals.Bangkok: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
capitals.Dili: Dili has a giant statue of Cristo Rei standing on a hill above the sea.
capitals.Ankara: Ankara gave its old name, Angora, to fluffy Angora goats, cats and rabbits.
capitals.Ashgabat: Ashgabat holds a world record for having the most buildings covered in white marble.
capitals.Abu Dhabi: Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque has one of the biggest hand-knotted carpets in the world.
capitals.Tashkent: Tashkent's metro stations are decorated like palaces, with chandeliers and mosaics.
capitals.Hanoi: Hanoi's Hoàn Kiếm Lake has a little temple on an island, and the city is famous for its pho.
capitals.Sanaa: Sanaa's old city has tall houses decorated with white patterns that look like gingerbread.
capitals.Tirana: Tirana is known for its brightly painted buildings and its big central Skanderbeg Square.
capitals.Andorra la Vella: Andorra la Vella is the highest capital city in Europe.
capitals.Vienna: Vienna is called the 'City of Music,' where Mozart and Beethoven worked, and it's famous for its cafés and cakes.
capitals.Minsk: Minsk is known for its wide avenues and its National Library, shaped like a giant diamond.
capitals.Brussels: Brussels is home to the Atomium, a giant shiny model of an atom, and it's famous for waffles.
capitals.Sarajevo: Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics and is famous for its old bazaar, Baščaršija.
capitals.Sofia: Sofia sits at the foot of Mount Vitosha, so people can go hiking and skiing right near the city.
capitals.Zagreb: Zagreb's St. Mark's Church has a colorful tiled roof decorated with coats of arms.
capitals.Nicosia: Nicosia's old town is surrounded by star-shaped walls built about 450 years ago.
capitals.Prague: Prague's astronomical clock has been ticking since 1410, making it one of the oldest working clocks of its kind.
capitals.Copenhagen: Copenhagen is home to Tivoli Gardens, one of the oldest amusement parks in the world, and the Little Mermaid statue.
capitals.Tallinn: Tallinn's old town is one of the best-preserved medieval towns in Europe.
capitals.Helsinki: Helsinki is surrounded by more than 300 islands, and one of them holds a whole sea fortress, Suomenlinna.
capitals.Paris: Paris is home to the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre, the world's most visited art museum, where the Mona Lisa hangs.
capitals.Berlin: Berlin has more bridges than Venice and is famous for the Brandenburg Gate.
capitals.Athens: Athens is one of the oldest cities in the world, crowned by the Parthenon temple on the Acropolis hill.
capitals.Budapest: Budapest was once two cities, Buda and Pest, on either side of the Danube. It's famous for its warm thermal baths.
capitals.Reykjavík: Reykjavík is the northernmost capital of a country, and many of its homes are heated by natural hot water from underground.
capitals.Dublin: Dublin's Trinity College holds the Book of Kells, a beautifully decorated book more than 1,200 years old.
capitals.Rome: Rome is home to the Colosseum, and visitors toss coins into the Trevi Fountain for good luck.
capitals.Pristina: Pristina's NEWBORN monument is a giant word sculpture that gets a fresh paint design every year.
capitals.Riga: Riga is famous for its Art Nouveau buildings and says it decorated the world's first Christmas tree, in 1510.
capitals.Vaduz: Vaduz has a real castle on the hill above town where the Prince of Liechtenstein lives.
capitals.Vilnius: Vilnius has one of the biggest old towns in Eastern Europe, and hot air balloons often float over it.
capitals.Luxembourg City: Luxembourg City is built on cliffs and has miles of old tunnels called casemates that you can explore.
capitals.Skopje: Skopje is the birthplace of Mother Teresa, famous for helping people in need, and has a museum about her life.
capitals.Valletta: Valletta is one of the smallest capitals in Europe and was built by the Knights of St. John in the 1500s.
capitals.Chișinău: Chișinău is one of the greenest cities in Europe, full of parks and trees.
capitals.Monaco: Monaco's Oceanographic Museum, built into a cliff above the sea, was once led by ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau.
capitals.Podgorica: Podgorica sits where the Ribnica and Morača rivers meet, surrounded by mountains.
capitals.Amsterdam: Amsterdam has more bicycles than people and about 165 canals.
capitals.Oslo: Oslo is where the Nobel Peace Prize is awarded every year.
capitals.Warsaw: Warsaw was the hometown of composer Frédéric Chopin and scientist Marie Curie, who won two Nobel Prizes.
capitals.Lisbon: Lisbon is built on seven hills and is famous for its yellow trams and custard tarts called pastéis de nata.
capitals.Bucharest: Bucharest's Palace of the Parliament is one of the heaviest buildings in the world.
capitals.Moscow: Moscow's Red Square and the colorful onion domes of St. Basil's Cathedral are world famous.
capitals.San Marino: The city of San Marino sits on top of Mount Titano, with three towers on its peaks.
capitals.Belgrade: Belgrade sits where the Sava and Danube rivers meet, below a big hilltop fortress park.
capitals.Bratislava: Bratislava is the only capital that borders two other countries, Austria and Hungary.
capitals.Ljubljana: Ljubljana's symbol is a dragon, and dragon statues guard its famous Dragon Bridge.
capitals.Madrid: Madrid's Prado Museum is one of the world's great art museums, and churros dipped in hot chocolate are a favorite treat.
capitals.Stockholm: Stockholm is built on 14 islands and is where most of the Nobel Prizes are handed out each year.
capitals.Bern: Switzerland calls Bern its 'federal city.' Its Zytglogge clock tower has moving figures that perform on the hour.
capitals.Kyiv: Kyiv's St. Sophia Cathedral has golden domes and mosaics almost 1,000 years old.
capitals.London: London's Big Ben is the nickname of the giant bell in its famous clock tower, and it has the world's oldest underground railway.
capitals.Vatican City: Vatican City is a country and a capital in one, and Michelangelo painted the famous Sistine Chapel ceiling here.
capitals.St. John's: St. John's is a colorful harbor town with a white cathedral looking out over the sea.
capitals.Nassau: Nassau's Queen's Staircase has 66 steps carved out of solid limestone rock.
capitals.Bridgetown: Bridgetown and its old Garrison area are a World Heritage Site with colorful colonial buildings.
capitals.Belmopan: Belmopan is one of the smallest capitals in the Americas, built inland among green hills in the 1970s.
capitals.Ottawa: In winter, Ottawa's Rideau Canal becomes one of the biggest skating rinks in the world.
capitals.San José: San José sits in a green valley surrounded by volcanoes and coffee farms.
capitals.Havana: Havana's old town is famous for colorful buildings and classic American cars from the 1950s.
capitals.Roseau: Roseau is a small, colorful harbor town near hot springs and waterfalls.
capitals.Santo Domingo: Santo Domingo, founded in 1496, is the oldest European-built city in the Americas.
capitals.San Salvador: San Salvador sits beside a volcano in a valley nicknamed the 'Valley of the Hammocks.'
capitals.St. George's: St. George's has a horseshoe-shaped harbor that's one of the prettiest in the Caribbean.
capitals.Guatemala City: Guatemala City is the biggest city in Central America and has a giant relief map of the country you can walk around.
capitals.Port-au-Prince: Port-au-Prince's Iron Market is a famous red market hall full of art and crafts.
capitals.Tegucigalpa: Tegucigalpa sits in a valley surrounded by mountains and pine forests.
capitals.Kingston: Kingston is home to the Bob Marley Museum, in the house where the reggae legend lived.
capitals.Mexico City: Mexico City was built on a lake by the Aztecs and is one of the biggest cities in the world. Its tacos al pastor are famous.
capitals.Managua: Managua sits on the shore of Lake Managua, with volcanoes close by.
capitals.Panama City: Panama City has a rainforest park full of sloths and toucans just minutes from its downtown skyscrapers.
capitals.Basseterre: Basseterre's Circus is a little roundabout with a clock tower, modeled on Piccadilly Circus in London.
capitals.Castries: Castries has a busy market where you can buy cocoa, spices and bananas.
capitals.Kingstown: Kingstown has the oldest botanical gardens in the Western Hemisphere, started in 1765.
capitals.Port of Spain: Port of Spain hosts one of the biggest Carnival celebrations in the world every year.
Washington, D.C. is home to the White House and the free Smithsonian museums, and it isn't part of any state.
capitals.Buenos Aires: Buenos Aires is the birthplace of the tango and has one of the widest avenues in the world, 9 de Julio Avenue.
capitals.Sucre: Sucre is Bolivia's official capital, but the government sits in La Paz. It's called the 'White City' for its white buildings.
capitals.Brasília: Brasília was built from scratch and became Brazil's capital in 1960. From above, its layout looks like an airplane.
capitals.Santiago: Santiago sits in a valley with the snowcapped Andes mountains rising right behind it.
capitals.Bogotá: Bogotá sits high in the Andes, and every Sunday it closes many streets so people can bike and skate.
capitals.Quito: Quito's old town was one of the very first places named a World Heritage Site, and the equator is just north of the city.
capitals.Georgetown: Georgetown's St. George's Cathedral is one of the tallest wooden churches in the world.
capitals.Asunción: Asunción, founded in 1537, is one of the oldest cities in South America.
capitals.Lima: Lima is famous for ceviche and is called one of the food capitals of the world.
capitals.Paramaribo: Paramaribo's historic center is a World Heritage Site full of white wooden buildings.
capitals.Montevideo: Montevideo's Rambla is a seaside walkway that runs for about 14 miles along the water.
capitals.Caracas: Caracas sits in a valley beneath Ávila Mountain, which you can ride to the top of in a cable car.
capitals.Canberra: Canberra was purpose-built as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.
capitals.Suva: Suva is one of the biggest cities in the South Pacific islands, on a peninsula with a large harbor.
capitals.Tarawa: Tarawa is a narrow coral atoll, so in many places you can see the ocean on both sides of the road.
capitals.Majuro: Majuro is a ring-shaped coral atoll, with one long road running along its thin strip of land.
capitals.Palikir: Palikir is a small capital in the green hills of Pohnpei, one of the rainiest places on Earth.
capitals.Yaren: Nauru has no official capital, but its government offices are in the Yaren District.
capitals.Wellington: Wellington is the southernmost capital city of a country, and it's famous for being windy.
capitals.Ngerulmud: Ngerulmud is one of the smallest capitals in the world, with its government building on a quiet hilltop.
capitals.Port Moresby: Port Moresby has a nature park full of colorful birds-of-paradise and tree kangaroos.
capitals.Apia: Apia is near the old home of Robert Louis Stevenson, the author of Treasure Island.
capitals.Honiara: Honiara is on Guadalcanal, the biggest of the Solomon Islands.
capitals.Nukuʻalofa: Nukuʻalofa is home to Tonga's Royal Palace, a white wooden building beside the sea.
capitals.Funafuti: Funafuti is a skinny coral atoll, and when no planes are coming, its airport runway becomes a playground.
capitals.Port Vila: Port Vila sits on a beautiful harbor, and divers can mail postcards from Vanuatu's underwater post office nearby.

stateCapitals.Montgomery, Alabama: Montgomery was home to Rosa Parks, whose brave bus ride in 1955 helped start the civil rights movement.
stateCapitals.Juneau, Alaska: Juneau is the only US state capital you can't drive to; people arrive by plane or boat.
stateCapitals.Phoenix, Arizona: Phoenix gets about 300 sunny days a year, and the Grand Canyon is a few hours north.
stateCapitals.Little Rock, Arkansas: Little Rock is named after a small rock on the bank of the Arkansas River that early travelers used as a landmark.
stateCapitals.Sacramento, California: Sacramento boomed during the California Gold Rush of 1849.
stateCapitals.Denver, Colorado: Denver is the 'Mile High City.' One step of its capitol building sits exactly one mile above sea level.
stateCapitals.Hartford, Connecticut: Hartford was home to author Mark Twain, who wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer there.
stateCapitals.Dover, Delaware: Delaware was the first state to approve the US Constitution, so it's nicknamed 'The First State.'
stateCapitals.Tallahassee, Florida: Tallahassee became the capital because it was halfway between Florida's two biggest cities at the time, Pensacola and St. Augustine.
stateCapitals.Atlanta, Georgia: Atlanta is the birthplace of Martin Luther King Jr. and home to one of the busiest airports in the world.
stateCapitals.Honolulu, Hawaii: Honolulu is home to Iolani Palace, the only royal palace in the United States.
stateCapitals.Boise, Idaho: Boise is called the 'City of Trees,' and Idaho grows about a third of America's potatoes.
stateCapitals.Springfield, Illinois: Springfield was Abraham Lincoln's hometown before he became president.
stateCapitals.Indianapolis, Indiana: Indianapolis hosts the Indy 500, one of the biggest one-day sporting events in the world.
stateCapitals.Des Moines, Iowa: Des Moines hosts the Iowa State Fair, famous for a life-size cow sculpted out of butter.
stateCapitals.Topeka, Kansas: Topeka's State Capitol dome is even taller than the US Capitol in Washington, D.C.
stateCapitals.Frankfort, Kentucky: Frankfort sits in Kentucky's Bluegrass region, famous for its horse farms.
stateCapitals.Baton Rouge, Louisiana: Baton Rouge means 'red stick' in French, and Louisiana's State Capitol is the tallest in the US.
stateCapitals.Augusta, Maine: Augusta sits on the Kennebec River, and Maine is famous for lobster and wild blueberries.
stateCapitals.Annapolis, Maryland: Annapolis is home to the US Naval Academy and was briefly the capital of the whole country in 1783 and 1784.
stateCapitals.Boston, Massachusetts: Boston has America's oldest public park, Boston Common, and the country's first subway.
stateCapitals.Lansing, Michigan: Lansing is where Ransom Olds started building Oldsmobile cars in 1897.
stateCapitals.Saint Paul, Minnesota: Saint Paul and Minneapolis are the Twin Cities, and Saint Paul throws a giant Winter Carnival with ice palaces.
stateCapitals.Jackson, Mississippi: Mississippi is the birthplace of the blues, and Jackson's museums celebrate the state's music.
stateCapitals.Jefferson City, Missouri: Jefferson City is named after President Thomas Jefferson and sits on the Missouri River.
stateCapitals.Helena, Montana: Helena was founded during a gold rush, and its main street is still called Last Chance Gulch.
stateCapitals.Lincoln, Nebraska: Lincoln's State Capitol is a tall tower nicknamed the 'Tower on the Plains.'
stateCapitals.Carson City, Nevada: Carson City is named after Kit Carson, a famous frontier scout and explorer.
stateCapitals.Concord, New Hampshire: Concord's capitol is the oldest in the US where lawmakers still meet in their original rooms.
stateCapitals.Trenton, New Jersey: A big sign on Trenton's bridge says 'Trenton Makes, The World Takes,' from its days as a busy factory city.
stateCapitals.Santa Fe, New Mexico: Santa Fe, founded around 1610, is the oldest state capital in the US and also the highest, at about 7,000 feet.
stateCapitals.Albany, New York: Albany is one of the oldest cities in the US, first settled by the Dutch in the 1600s.
stateCapitals.Raleigh, North Carolina: Raleigh is called the 'City of Oaks' for all its leafy oak trees.
stateCapitals.Bismarck, North Dakota: Bismarck sits on the Missouri River, not far from where explorers Lewis and Clark spent a winter.
stateCapitals.Columbus, Ohio: Columbus is home to Ohio State University and one of the biggest zoos in the country.
stateCapitals.Oklahoma City, Oklahoma: Oklahoma City's State Capitol is the only one with oil wells on its grounds.
stateCapitals.Salem, Oregon: Oregon's capitol in Salem is topped with a gold-covered statue of a pioneer.
stateCapitals.Harrisburg, Pennsylvania: Pennsylvania's capitol in Harrisburg has a dome inspired by St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
stateCapitals.Providence, Rhode Island: Providence hosts WaterFire, when bonfires are lit on its rivers at night with music playing.
stateCapitals.Columbia, South Carolina: Columbia was one of the first planned capital cities in the US, laid out in 1786.
stateCapitals.Pierre, South Dakota: Pierre is one of the smallest state capitals, and Mount Rushmore is a few hours west.
stateCapitals.Nashville, Tennessee: Nashville is called 'Music City' and is the home of country music.
stateCapitals.Austin, Texas: Austin is the 'Live Music Capital of the World,' and over a million bats live under one of its bridges.
stateCapitals.Salt Lake City, Utah: Salt Lake City hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics, and the Great Salt Lake nearby is saltier than the ocean.
stateCapitals.Montpelier, Vermont: Montpelier is the smallest state capital in the US, and Vermont makes more maple syrup than any other state.
stateCapitals.Richmond, Virginia: Richmond has whitewater rapids on the James River, right in the middle of the city.
stateCapitals.Olympia, Washington: Olympia sits at the southern tip of Puget Sound, with views of the Olympic Mountains.
stateCapitals.Charleston, West Virginia: Charleston's capitol dome is covered in real gold leaf.
stateCapitals.Madison, Wisconsin: Madison is built on a narrow strip of land between two big lakes.
stateCapitals.Cheyenne, Wyoming: Cheyenne hosts Frontier Days, one of the biggest outdoor rodeos in the world.
